lessons.title: Dinosaurs Lived a Long Time Ago
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say that dinosaurs lived a very long time ago and no longer exist.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss that dinosaurs lived millions of years ago and are now extinct, introducing the idea of a very long time ago.
key_questions: When did dinosaurs live?
Are there dinosaurs alive today?

differentiation.extension: Discuss what 'extinct' means in more detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of deep time/history — evidence for UTW.1.
lessons.home_link: Look at a dinosaur book or picture together.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Harry and the Bucketful of Dinosaurs'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name Harry's favourite dinosaur toys.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story, discussing Harry's dinosaur toys and the adventure.
key_questions: What are Harry's dinosaur toys called?
What happens in the story?

differentiation.extension: Retell part of the story in own words

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and recall — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Discuss favourite part of the story.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Counting Dinosaur Eggs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count dinosaur egg counters accurately up to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Count a nest of egg pictures together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and sort dinosaur egg counters into nests, recording totals.
key_questions: How many eggs are in this nest?
Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.

lessons.title: Making a Dinosaur Craft
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple dinosaur model using craft materials.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at dinosaur pictures noting different features.
lessons.main_activity: Children make a dinosaur craft using paper/card, adding texture for scales/spikes.
resources_needed: Card, paint, craft materials for texture
key_questions: What dinosaur are you making?
How did you show the scales/spikes?

differentiation.extension: Design own dinosaur shape and add detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor and creative texture representation — evidence for EAD.1/PD.2.
lessons.home_link: Draw your own dinosaur together at home.

lessons.title: Herbivores and Carnivores
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort dinosaurs into meat-eaters and plant-eaters.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what different dinosaurs might have eaten based on their teeth (pictures).
lessons.main_activity: Sort dinosaur picture cards into herbivore (plant-eater) and carnivore (meat-eater) groups, discussing teeth/features that show this.
key_questions: What did this dinosaur eat?
How can you tell from its teeth?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early scientific categorisation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look up what a favourite dinosaur ate together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'ng' Digraph
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the digraph sound 'ng' and blend words (ring, sing, king).
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'ng' digraph sound/action; blend new words.
key_questions: What sound do these two letters make?
Can you blend r-i-ng?
lessons.plenary: Practise all four digraphs learned so far.

lessons.title: Comparing Dinosaur Sizes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and order dinosaurs by size.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a size comparison chart of different dinosaurs.
lessons.main_activity: Children order dinosaur picture cutouts from smallest to biggest, using comparative language.
resources_needed: Dinosaur picture cutouts of varying sizes
key_questions: Which dinosaur is biggest?
Can you order them all?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note size-ordering skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of dinosaur size order.
lessons.home_link: Compare sizes of toy dinosaurs or other toys at home.

lessons.title: Moving Like Dinosaurs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move imaginatively like different sized/types of dinosaurs.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how a huge dinosaur might move vs a small quick one.
lessons.main_activity: Children move around the space imitating stomping herbivores, prowling carnivores, and flying pterosaurs.
key_questions: How does a big dinosaur move?
Can you move like a flying dinosaur?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative movement — evidence for EAD.2/PD.1.
lessons.home_link: Act out a dinosaur movement for family.

lessons.title: What Are Fossils?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain simply that fossils are how we learn about dinosaurs.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of real fossils.
lessons.main_activity: Children explore a simple 'fossil dig' (objects hidden in sand/flour) and discuss how scientists find fossils to learn about dinosaurs.
resources_needed: Sand/flour tray, small toy bones/shapes to 'excavate'
key_questions: What did you find in your dig?
How do fossils help us learn about dinosaurs?

differentiation.extension: Explain the process of becoming a fossil simply

lessons.assessment_notes: Note investigative engagement and understanding — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap what a fossil is and why they're important.
lessons.home_link: Look up a picture of a real dinosaur fossil together.

lessons.title: Writing Dinosaur Names
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple dinosaur name.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap dinosaur names learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Children choose a favourite dinosaur and attempt to write its name (e.g. T-Rex) using known phonics sounds.
resources_needed: Paper, pencils, dinosaur name cards for reference
key_questions: Which dinosaur are you writing about?
Can you write its name?

differentiation.extension: Independent phonetic attempts at longer names

lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share dinosaur name writing with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Practise writing a dinosaur name together at home.

lessons.title: Measuring Dinosaur Footprints
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure and compare footprint sizes using non-standard units.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture comparing a dinosaur footprint to a human footprint.
lessons.main_activity: Children measure paper dinosaur footprint cutouts using linking cubes/hand spans, comparing to their own footprint.
key_questions: How many cubes long is this footprint?
Is it bigger or smaller than your foot?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early measurement skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Measure your own footprint at home using any small objects.

lessons.title: Where Did Dinosaurs Live?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a habitat where dinosaurs might have lived.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of prehistoric landscapes.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss different environments dinosaurs may have lived in (swamps, forests, deserts), matching dinosaurs to likely habitats.
resources_needed: Prehistoric landscape and dinosaur picture cards
key_questions: Where do you think this dinosaur lived?
Why might it live there?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of habitats — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look up where a favourite dinosaur lived together.

lessons.title: Retelling 'Harry and the Bucketful of Dinosaurs'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words and toy dinosaurs as props.
key_questions: What happened first?
What happened at the end?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Number Bonds Recap: Dinosaur Egg Theme
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall number bonds to 10 fluently.
lessons.main_activity: Using dinosaur egg counters split between two nests, children practise and record all number bonds to 10.
key_questions: What are all the ways to make 10?
Can you recall this without counting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond to 10 fluency — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 10.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 10 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Dinosaur Roar Song and Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sing a dinosaur-themed song with actions and expressive sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Learn a simple dinosaur song with actions and roaring sounds, performing with confidence.
key_questions: What action goes with this line?
Can you make a big roar?

differentiation.extension: Suggest and lead a new action

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe participation and expressive movement/sound — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.home_link: Sing the dinosaur song for family.

lessons.title: Dinosaurs Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about dinosaurs learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Dinosaurs' display summarising diet, habitat, and fossil learning.
key_questions: What have we learned about dinosaurs?
What was most interesting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about dinosaurs with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: All Digraphs (ch, sh, th, ng)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words using all digraphs learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building with all digraphs, reading cards, simple sentence reading (e.g. 'the king can sing').
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?
Can you read this sentence?

differentiation.support: Build/read simple digraph words with support
differentiation.extension: Read sentences with multiple digraphs independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise Spring 1 digraph phonics tracker for 'ch', 'sh', 'th', 'ng'.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all digraphs learned with a reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading words with digraphs over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Spring 1 Half-Term Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to demonstrate progress across the half-term's key maths skills.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap key maths learning from across Spring 1.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through stations reviewing counting backwards, measuring, ordering by size, and number bonds to 10 from across the half-term.
resources_needed: Station resources from across the half-term
key_questions: What have you learned this half-term in maths?
What are you most proud of?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise Spring 1 maths progress overall — evidence for MATHS.1/MATHS.2 across the half-term.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate everyone's maths progress this half-term.
lessons.home_link: Practise favourite maths games together over half-term break.

lessons.title: Dinosaur Celebration Performance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform the week's song/movement with confidence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance combining the dinosaur song and movements, with craft dinosaurs displayed.
resources_needed: Craft from the week, music player
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this half-term?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment across Spring 1 EAD learning — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; celebrate a fantastic Spring 1 half-term.
lessons.home_link: Perform the dinosaur song for family over the half-term break.
